historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Historical growth rates are not suitable as DCF anchors. The 5yr revenue CAGR of 20.3% reflects exceptional 2020-2025 hypergrowth that has structurally decelerated. The 3yr revenue CAGR of 11.0% is closer to current reality but still overstates the near-term outlook. FY2026 management guidance calls for only +2-4% revenue growth. FCF CAGRs are distorted: the 3yr is inflated by a depressed FY2022 base (capex surge, $327.8M FCF), while the 5yr (9.9%) is dragged down by FY2025 tariff impacts ($275M gross). Equity CAGR (14.2% 5yr) is understated because $1.2B+/yr in share buybacks reduces reported book value mechanically. The DCF uses the 3yr revenue CAGR (11.0%) as a reference point but anchors scenario growth rates to management guidance and the FCF recovery trajectory from the current tariff-depressed trough.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FCF CAGR divergence is significant and explained: FY2022 FCF of $327.8M was a trough (inventory build + capex surge), inflating the 3yr FCF CAGR to 41.1%. FY2025 FCF of $921.7M is a new trough from $275M gross tariff impact. Neither endpoint is representative. Revenue and equity CAGRs (11-20% range) are more reliable but overstate the near-term outlook given FY2026 guidance of +2-4%. No structural divergence concern; discrepancies are event-driven.

historical_fcf_series.note: FY2022 depressed by capex surge and inventory build. FY2025 depressed by $275M gross tariff hit. Pre-tariff normalized FCF (average FY2022-FY2024) approx $1,185M.

base.name: Base Case: Gradual Recovery + China Offset
base.description: FY2026 FCF declines further as the tariff headwind worsens from $275M to $380M gross ($220M net). From FY2027, supply chain diversification (shifting from Vietnam to Bangladesh/Indonesia/India) progressively reduces tariff drag. China Mainland sustains ~20% growth, approaching $1.5B+ revenue. Americas stabilizes in H2 FY2026 and inflects positive in FY2027 under a new permanent CEO. FCF recovers toward $1.2-1.5B range by FY2030 as tariff drag diminishes and operating leverage returns.
base.growth_rate_reasoning: Y1 (-10%): FY2026 tariff escalation ($380M gross vs $275M) and continued Americas weakness causes FCF to fall from $921.7M to ~$829.5M despite $160M in management-guided cost offsets and continued buybacks. Y2 (+15%): Supply chain shifts begin contributing; China ~$1.4B+ at 20% growth adds earnings mix; new CEO likely in place. Y3 (+20%): Tariff drag meaningfully reduces as Vietnam concentration falls from 40% toward 25%; Americas returns to positive comps. Y4 (+15%): Operating leverage as revenue grows faster than fixed costs; China approaching $2B. Y5 (+12%): Sustainable growth normalizes as the business rebuilds toward pre-tariff FCF levels.
base.wacc_reasoning: CAPM: risk-free rate 4.3% + equity risk premium 5.0% × beta 1.1 = ~9.8%, rounded to 10%. Beta of 1.1 reflects consumer discretionary cyclicality and elevated uncertainty (CEO transition, proxy fight, tariff exposure). No debt means WACC equals cost of equity.

bull.name: Bull Case: Turnaround Succeeds + New CEO Re-rates
bull.description: A transformational permanent CEO (potentially Elliott-backed Jane Nielsen or similar) is appointed by mid-FY2026 and restores strategic clarity. Spring 2026 product reset (35% new styles) stabilizes Americas comps faster than expected, turning positive by Q3 FY2026. US-Vietnam trade tensions ease in FY2027 as part of broader trade negotiations, removing the largest tariff cost (~40% of product). China accelerates toward 25%+ as the store count approaches 200 and men's penetration deepens. FCF rapidly recovers toward $2B+ by FY2030 as tariff drag reverses and top-line momentum returns.
bull.growth_rate_reasoning: Y1 (0%): Management efficiency gains exactly offset the incremental tariff headwind; FCF flat at $921.7M. Y2 (+30%): New CEO appointment triggers investor confidence; Americas inflects positive; tariff relief begins. Y3 (+30%): Supply chain fully diversified; operating leverage accelerates; China approaching $2B. Y4 (+20%): International revenue becomes ~35%+ of total; strong FCF conversion on mature market base. Y5 (+15%): Sustained compound growth as men's and footwear categories scale.
bull.wacc_reasoning: Lower WACC of 9% justified by resolved governance uncertainty (permanent CEO in place), reduced tariff risk, and strengthening balance sheet. Implies a slightly lower risk premium on a recovered, better-positioned business.

bear.name: Bear Case: Structural Americas Decline + Tariff Persistence
bear.description: The Americas comparable sales decline proves structural rather than cyclical — Alo Yoga and Vuori have permanently captured a portion of LULU's customer base, and the premium athleisure wallet is satiated. CEO search extends into FY2027 while the proxy fight consumes governance bandwidth. Tariffs remain elevated through FY2029 as supply chain diversification is slower than expected. China growth decelerates to ~10-12% as domestic brand competition intensifies and geopolitical tensions weigh on Western brand sentiment. FCF remains trapped in the $700-900M range with no structural catalyst for recovery.
bear.growth_rate_reasoning: Y1 (-15%): FY2026 is worse than FY2025 — tariffs increase, Americas revenue declines, proxy contest costs, incentive compensation reinstatement. FCF drops to ~$783M. Y2 (+5%): Minimal recovery; CEO search still unresolved; Americas comps still negative. Y3-Y4 (+8%): Marginal improvement as China sustains low-teens growth and some supply chain shifts reduce tariff exposure. Y5 (+7%): Terminal growth rate approaching as the business settles at permanently lower profitability level. Americas never meaningfully recovers.
bear.wacc_reasoning: Higher WACC of 11% reflects: elevated governance risk with no permanent CEO, structural competitive concerns about Americas brand health, persistent tariff headwind uncertainty, and higher required return premium for a business with declining profitability trajectory. Still reflects zero-debt balance sheet as a partial offset.

base.interpretation: At $127.18, an investor is paying 51% above the base case 15%-CAGR entry price of $84.12. This reflects that the market is already pricing in some recovery — the current price is not a distressed value entry. A 15% annualized return in the base case requires a significantly lower entry point (~$84) or the bull case materializing.

bull.interpretation: In the bull case, the current price of $127.18 is 17% below the $154.05 entry price required for a 15% CAGR. If the turnaround scenario materializes, the current price offers an attractive entry — one of the few scenarios where LULU represents a compelling risk-adjusted return.

bear.interpretation: In the bear case, the current price is 162% above the entry price needed for a 15% CAGR to terminal value. If structural decline materializes, returns from current levels would be significantly negative.

sensitivity.matrix_note: All cells use base case FCF growth rates [-10%, +15%, +20%, +15%, +12%] starting from FY2025 base FCF of $921.7M. Rows = WACC (8-12%), Columns = Terminal Growth Rate (2.0-4.0%). Values are intrinsic value per share in USD. Current price of $127.18 is bracketed between WACC 11% (TG 2-3% range: $132-144) and WACC 12% (TG 3-4% range: $129-140), suggesting the market is implicitly pricing approximately an 11-12% WACC with 2.5-3% terminal growth — consistent with the current uncertainty premium.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Base case carries 50% weight as the most probable outcome — gradual recovery over 3-5 years as supply chain diversification reduces tariffs and a new CEO stabilizes Americas. Bull case at 25% reflects that LULU's brand moat (55%+ gross margins, DTC model, China momentum) is durable and activist pressure (Elliott + Chip Wilson) may accelerate a credible turnaround. Bear case at 25% reflects genuine structural risk: eight consecutive quarters of Americas comp declines, the durability of which is not yet disproved. The bear case weight is held at 25% rather than higher because: (1) the net cash position ($1.81B, zero debt) limits catastrophic downside; (2) China's 29% FY2025 growth and 20% FY2026 guidance is a real and growing offset; (3) premium brand equity with 55%+ gross margins does not evaporate quickly.

valuation_philosophy.approach: This DCF uses FY2025 FCF of $921.7M as the base — a tariff-depressed trough. The model's primary analytical task is to assess whether and how quickly FCF recovers toward the pre-tariff normalized level (~$1.2-1.6B). The base case embeds a full recovery by FY2028-2029 as supply chain diversification and China growth compound. The bear case treats the $700-900M FCF range as a new semi-permanent floor. Because LULU has zero long-term debt and $1.81B in cash, the equity value floor is meaningfully supported — the bear case intrinsic value of $100.56 represents a ~21% downside from current prices, not a wipeout scenario.
valuation_philosophy.fcf_vs_earnings_note: FCF is a better valuation anchor than EPS for LULU because: (1) FY2025 net income of $1,579.2M vs FCF of $921.7M reflects $680.8M in capital expenditures (store expansion, supply chain infrastructure); (2) CapEx is expected to remain elevated at $725-745M in FY2026; (3) FCF captures the true cash-generative capacity after reinvestment. However, CapEx is partially discretionary — the company could reduce store expansion to boost FCF in a capital-allocation pivot.
valuation_philosophy.buyback_effect: LULU's $1.2B/yr share buyback program is a meaningful capital return mechanism that reduces share count ~2%/yr. This creates a structural EPS tailwind even in flat revenue environments. The buybacks also reduce reported book value, making P/B comparisons to historical ranges misleading. Shareholders' equity would be approximately $6-8B higher (at ~$50-65/share) without the cumulative buyback program.
valuation_philosophy.sensitivity_interpretation: The sensitivity matrix shows that at the base case growth assumptions, the stock is broadly fairly valued across most WACC/terminal growth combinations. Current price of $127.18 plots approximately at WACC 11-12% and terminal growth 2.5-3.0%. The matrix implies limited margin of safety at current entry unless the base or bull case materializes. The bull case entry price ($154) is above current price, making today's price an attractive entry ONLY IF the turnaround narrative proves credible.

historical_ranges.pb_note: P/B range understated by aggressive buybacks reducing book value; economic P/B is materially higher than accounting P/B

sanity_check.verdict: PASS with annotation. The base case IV of $155.63 implies 11.7x trailing P/E and 3.7x P/B — both below LULU's historical premium range but consistent with a genuine operational trough. The market itself is pricing LULU at 9.6x trailing P/E, already at historical lows, suggesting the stock IS in distressed-multiple territory. The base case IV is only 22% above current price, which is internally consistent: our model says LULU is modestly undervalued rather than deeply cheap, reflecting that the recovery is gradual and the risks are real. The bull case (20x P/E, 6.4x P/B) represents a realistic premium-brand re-rating if the turnaround succeeds. The bear case (7.6x P/E) implies permanent impairment — plausible but not the base expectation. P/B values appear low vs historical norms due to buyback distortion; economic P/B adjusted for cumulative repurchases would be approximately 1.5-2x higher across all scenarios.

key_assumptions_summary.wacc_chosen: 10% base, 9% bull, 11% bear. CAPM-derived (rf 4.3% + ERP 5.0% × beta 1.1 = 9.8%) rounded to 10%. Beta of 1.1 captures consumer discretionary cyclicality and governance uncertainty. No leverage adjustment needed (zero debt).
key_assumptions_summary.terminal_growth_chosen: 2.5% base, 3.0% bull, 2.0% bear. Below nominal GDP growth of ~4% (2-2.5% real + 2% inflation), which is appropriate for a mature premium apparel company with structural competitive threats in its core market. China growth provides an above-GDP tailwind that partially offsets Americas maturity.
key_assumptions_summary.base_fcf_note: FY2025 FCF of $921.7M is used as base despite being tariff-depressed ($275M gross tariff impact). This is intentionally conservative: the model must demonstrate that FCF recovery justifies current valuations rather than assuming a normalized base. Year 1 projects further decline to ~$829.5M as FY2026 tariff worsens to $380M gross.
key_assumptions_summary.recovery_path_logic: Supply chain diversification from Vietnam (~40% of product) takes 2-3 years. Bangladesh, Indonesia, and India sourcing expansion reduces the Vietnam tariff exposure progressively. By FY2028 (Y3), we model meaningful tariff drag reduction. China reaching $2B+ revenue by FY2028-2029 provides margin mix improvement as international margins are above company average.
key_assumptions_summary.net_cash_significance: The $1.81B net cash position (zero debt) adds $15.17/share in direct equity value above the DCF value of operations. This provides a meaningful floor under the intrinsic value calculation and is a key reason the bear case ($100.56) does not reflect catastrophic downside despite operational challenges.

valuation_context.ev_ebitda_note: Approximate EBITDA FY2025: operating income $2,210.6M + est. D&A ~$330M = ~$2,540M. EV/EBITDA at current price ~5.2x — historically very cheap for LULU (normal range 12-25x). This reinforces that the market is pricing in prolonged earnings pressure.
valuation_context.buyback_context: LULU has guided to ~$1.2B in FY2026 share repurchases (similar to FY2025 actual). At $127/share, this retires approximately 9.4M shares (~8% of outstanding). Share count could fall to ~112M by end FY2026, providing an EPS accretion tailwind that partially offsets the earnings decline from tariffs and lower revenue.
